decisions.statement: A HEAD of the root path is answered 200 with no body.
A GET of `/healthz` is answered 200 with the body `ok`.
A GET of `/inflight` is answered the count of requests in flight.
A GET of `/inflight` is answered the hold registry's count.
A GET of `/rc-status` is answered the count of remote-control connections.
A POST of `/v1/messages` is handed to the message handler.
A POST of `/v1/messages/count_tokens` is handed to the message handler.
A path no route here names is forwarded upstream.
A method a route does not name is forwarded upstream.
Every request is written about before a route is chosen.
The line written for a request says whether an authorization header arrived.
A request reaching the message handler is given no server timeout.
A request reaching the message handler raises the in-flight count.
A response with a body arms the observer to lower the in-flight count.
A response with no body lowers the in-flight count before that answer goes out.
A response leaving the slot empty lowers the in-flight count.
A slot holding an observer nothing armed is emptied.
A client that aborts ends the observer as a client disconnect.
A client that aborts lowers the in-flight count.
The in-flight count is lowered once however many ends are reached.
A request forwarded over the remote-control listener raises the connection count.
A request forwarded over the port raises no connection count.
A remote-control response with a body arms its observer to lower that count.
A remote-control request that aborts lowers the connection count.
A request with a body is read into one buffer before that request is forwarded.
A forwarded request carrying an authorization of its own is sent with no access token of its own.
A forwarded request carrying no authorization is sent with the credential of a picked account.
A forwarded request is sent with no access token where no account is left to choose.
The port is bound through `bind-with-retry`.
A listener answering no port is stopped.
A listener answering no port throws.
A unix socket path is cleared before the remote-control listener is opened.
A remote-control listener that throws leaves the port listener serving.
A remote-control listener that throws is written about on the warning seam.
Stopping a gateway stops the port listener.
Stopping a gateway stops the remote-control listener.
Stopping a gateway takes the unix socket path away.
The unix socket path goes away even where stopping that listener throws.
A gateway with no unix socket path takes no socket path away.
A flush ends every stream the shutdown registry has.
The port handed back is the port the listener bound.
The effects handed in are reached rather than effects built from the root.
The effects are built from the root where the caller hands no effects in.
The log prefix is `[oauth-proxy]` where the caller names no prefix.
An idle span the caller names nowhere reaches the forward as zero.
A keepalive span the caller names nowhere reaches the forward as zero.
The clock is handed in so a test needs no real time.
The sleep is handed in so a test needs no wait.
The fetch is handed in so a test needs no network.
The listener is handed in so a test needs no open socket.
Every line written here goes to a seam the caller may replace.
The pipeline a message turn runs through is named here.
A message turn is run through `pre-forward-queue`.
An attempt that queue makes is `account-walk`.
A queue that commits answers with `committed-keepalive`.
A queue that exhausts answers with `rate-limit-refusal`.
The account a request is sent under is chosen by `account-picker`.
The credential that account is sent with is read by `fresh-credential`.
One account picker is built for the life of a gateway.
A pipeline handed in replaces the pipeline named here.
A POST naming a stopped subagent is refused rather than handed to the message handler.
A POST of a messages path naming no subagent reaches the message handler whatever is held.
The subagents held as stopped are handed in, and none is held where none is handed in.
A turn refused as a stopped subagent's is written about as a 400.
A caller has the proxy starting a gateway hands back for as long as that gateway runs.
Nothing here chooses an account.
Nothing here reads a token.
Nothing here retries a request.
Nothing here writes a transport row.
Nothing here reads a clock the caller cannot replace.
No route here answers a credential.
Nothing here reads the `getLogDir` the start options carry.
The directory `getLogDir` answers is no page file a transport row lands beside.
Nothing here reads the refresh outcome hook the start options have.
Nothing here reads the terminal test the start options have.
A request whose url will not parse throws out of the route unanswered.
A request forwarded over the port leaves the observer of that request unended.
The routes are written here rather than handed in.
A socket path left over is kept where the remote-control listener never opened.
Nothing proves these routes against a listener that is really open.

definition: a gateway serving from its start to its stop
